concerns.concern: The headline performance claim rests on effective conductivity σeff, which is not a figure of merit. With S_SSE one to two orders of magnitude below Pt/YIG benchmarks, the power factor is no better than, or worse than, thin-film devices.
concerns.quote: The central performance claim rests on σeff, which is not a figure of merit, and no benchmark shows that trans-scaling improves output.

concerns.concern: No control experiment separates spin Seebeck from ordinary Nernst, thermal or impurity-ANE signals. In particular, there is no Pt-coated non-magnetic garnet (GGG or YAG) powder processed identically.
concerns.quote: no Pt-coated non-magnetic garnet (GGG or YAG powder) processed identically, which would bound Pt-only and processing-induced artifacts

concerns.concern: YIG was not coated with a metal of opposite spin Hall angle (W, Ta). The resulting sign reversal would be a fingerprint that impurity ANE cannot mimic.
concerns.quote: no YIG coated with an NM of opposite spin Hall angle (W, Ta), where sign reversal would be a fingerprint that impurity-phase ANE cannot mimic

concerns.concern: There is no control using YIG coated with a low spin-orbit metal (Cu, Al), where strong signal suppression is expected.
concerns.quote: no YIG coated with a low-SOC metal (Cu, Al), where strong suppression is expected

concerns.concern: The temperature dependence of the signal is not measured or compared with known YIG/Pt SSE behaviour.
concerns.quote: no temperature dependence compared with known YIG/Pt SSE behaviour

concerns.concern: The magnon-specific suppression of the signal at high fields (several tesla) is not tested.
concerns.quote: no high-field (several-tesla) magnon-specific suppression

concerns.concern: There are no null geometries (field parallel to voltage or to the gradient) and no field-angle rotation scans to verify E ∝ ∇T×M.
concerns.quote: no null geometries (H ∥ voltage direction; H ∥ ∇T) or field-angle rotation scans verifying E ∝ ∇T×M

concerns.concern: The sign of the signal is not checked against the established Pt/YIG convention or a reference bilayer.
concerns.quote: no check of the signal sign against the established Pt/YIG convention or a reference bilayer

concerns.concern: A minute ferromagnetic metallic phase (Fe, FePt or alloyed interfaces from interdiffusion or shear) could produce the ~10 nV/K signal. XRD, with its ~1–5 wt% detection limit and its admitted failure to distinguish α-Fe₂O₃ from YFeO₃, cannot exclude this.
concerns.quote: A signal of ~10 nV/K requires only a minute (≪1 vol%), possibly percolating or interfacial, ferromagnetic metallic phase

concerns.concern: Cobalt from the binder of the tungsten-carbide die may have transferred into the samples during compaction in air. This is not checked by EDX, ICP or XPS.
concerns.quote: Co transfer from the tungsten-carbide die (Co binder) during compaction in air.

concerns.concern: The argument that the drop in Ms after Pt deposition rules out a ferromagnetic metal is not a bound. Pt mass dilution can mask a small ferromagnetic fraction, so the expected dilution must be computed.
concerns.quote: "Ms decreases after Pt deposition, hence no FMM" fails because Pt mass dilution can mask a small FM fraction.

concerns.concern: The Hall test reports only a 'linear' result with large noise, and its detection limit is not converted into an ANE upper bound. A minority ferromagnetic phase could also have an ANE larger than its visible AHE.
concerns.quote: No detection limit is converted, e.g. via σxy/α relations, into an upper bound on ANE.

concerns.concern: The Hall test was done in a different apparatus at 100 mA through a porous network. Possible Joule heating and thermal artifacts are not addressed, and no current-reversal data are shown.
concerns.quote: It was performed in a different apparatus (CFMS), with possible Joule heating from 100 mA through a porous, partially percolating network.

concerns.concern: The known small SMR-related AHE-like signal of Pt/YIG is not seen. This suggests the Hall measurement lacks the sensitivity to detect a ferromagnetic metal.
concerns.quote: Its absence may indicate insufficient sensitivity rather than the absence of a ferromagnetic metal.

concerns.concern: No effective-medium, finite-element or network model predicts the composite S_SSE and σeff from known Pt/YIG parameters. Without one, readers cannot judge whether ~10 nV/K is consistent with SSE given orientation averaging, circulating currents and shunting.
concerns.quote: No effective-medium, finite-element or resistor-network model predicts the composite S_SSE and σeff from known Pt/YIG parameters.

concerns.concern: The defining 'trans-scale' volumetric mechanism is never tested. No experiment varies YIG particle size relative to the magnon diffusion length, or systematically varies Pt thickness and volume fraction.
concerns.quote: No experiment varies YIG particle size relative to λm (~10 µm), even though SEM suggests particles from sub-µm to tens of µm.

concerns.concern: The thermoelectric-conductivity product α_yx scales roughly fourfold with nominal Pt thickness. Interface-driven SSE would not do this, which points instead to percolation, shunting or a Pt-bulk contribution.
concerns.quote: For interface-driven SSE with t_Pt ≫ λs, α_yx should be set by interface area, not Pt thickness.

concerns.concern: S_SSE drops only ~15–20% when Pt thickness doubles, despite large changes in conductance. Calling this consistent with typical Pt thickness dependence is unjustified.
concerns.quote: Calling this "qualitatively consistent with the typical Pt thickness dependence" is not justified.

concerns.concern: Room-temperature-pressed samples give about twice the S_SSE of 300 °C samples. The causes (oxidation, interdiffusion, recrystallization, porosity) are not investigated.
concerns.quote: RT-pressed samples give ~2× larger S_SSE than 300 °C samples despite similar density

concerns.concern: The statement that Pt thicknesses well above the spin diffusion length 'ensure clear observation' is conceptually backwards, because thicker metal increases shunting.
concerns.quote: The claim that 15 and 30 nm are "well above λs, ensuring clear observation" is conceptually backwards

concerns.concern: The magnetization plots show ~0.02–0.04 emu/g while the text quotes 37.9 emu/g, an apparent units error of three orders of magnitude.
concerns.quote: Fig. 3f/S6 plots ~0.02–0.04 "emu/g", three orders of magnitude off, while the text quotes 37.9 emu/g.

concerns.concern: The reference Ms of 37.9 emu/g is YIG's 0 K value, not the ~27–28 emu/g room-temperature value.
concerns.quote: 37.9 emu/g corresponds to YIG's low-temperature (0 K) Ms. The room-temperature value is ~27–28 emu/g.

concerns.concern: Ms is reduced by ~20–25% almost equally for 15 nm and 30 nm Pt, which is inconsistent with mass dilution. This may indicate degraded YIG surfaces or normalization errors.
concerns.quote: The composites show a ~20–25% Ms reduction relative to the crystal that is nearly the same for 15 nm and 30 nm Pt.

concerns.concern: Shell thicknesses of 15/30 nm are inferred from deposition time. TEM exists only for as-coated 2.5/5 nm powders, and a thickness distribution is expected from sputtering onto a broad particle-size distribution.
concerns.quote: The 15/30 nm thicknesses are inferred from deposition time, assuming a linear rate.

concerns.concern: No cross-sectional TEM shows that the Pt shells survive high-pressure compaction. The µm-resolution SEM-EDX shows Pt-rich aggregates that suggest smearing or agglomeration.
concerns.quote: No cross-sectional TEM/STEM-EDS of the sintered 15/30 nm composites shows that shells remain continuous after 350–500 MPa compaction

concerns.concern: Key microstructural inputs are not reported: grain-size distribution after crushing, Pt mass or volume fraction, shell connectivity, and how porosity interrupts the shells.
concerns.quote: the Pt mass or volume fraction (likely a few percent; ~10 wt% estimated)

concerns.concern: σeff is far below what a connected Pt network should give, which suggests cracked shells or poor connectivity. This limits the power factor but is not analyzed.
concerns.quote: The measured 5×10²–5×10³ S/m suggests poor connectivity, cracked shells or high contact resistance.

concerns.concern: Isotropy is presented as distinctive of trans-scale SSE, but it is expected for random interfaces. It has the same symmetry as ANE from any isotropically distributed contaminant.
concerns.quote: This has exactly the symmetry of an ANE.

concerns.concern: The isotropy evidence comes from a single sample measured with two different thermal setups, so the agreement may be fortuitous. It should be repeated on all compositions and on one cube in three orientations.
concerns.quote: The 14.8 vs 14.4 nV/K agreement comes from a single sample (30-RT) measured with two different thermal setups

concerns.concern: Uniaxial pressing could make the Pt network anisotropic. The pressing-axis orientation and the direction in which σeff was measured are not stated, and σ and κ are not reported along both directions.
concerns.quote: Uniaxial pressing could produce anisotropic Pt connectivity. The relation of x, y, z to the pressing axis is not stated

concerns.concern: In one geometry the signal keeps rising up to 5–7 kOe while M(H) saturates by 1–2 kOe. This non-saturating component is neither identified nor separated.
concerns.quote: The non-saturating part (e.g., ordinary Nernst of the Pt network, or an unidentified phase) is neither identified nor separated.

concerns.concern: The M(H) measurement orientation, any demagnetization correction and the sample dimensions are not given. Field dependence therefore cannot be compared with magnetization in the same geometry.
concerns.quote: The M(H) measurement orientation and any demagnetization correction are not specified, and sample dimensions are given nowhere.

concerns.concern: The thermal gradient is inferred from the heat-bath temperature difference, which includes interfacial drops. The resulting error is never quantified, undermining absolute S_SSE values.
concerns.quote: It is inferred from the heat-bath ΔT, including interfacial drops, as the authors acknowledge. The error is argued to be smaller for low-κ samples but never quantified.

concerns.concern: The two measurement configurations use different contact schemes, and the thermal tape adds significant interfacial resistance.
concerns.quote: The two configurations use different contact schemes, and the thermal tape adds significant interfacial thermal resistance.

concerns.concern: Sample dimensions, electrode spacing and contact sizes are not reported.
concerns.quote: Sample dimensions Lx, Ly, Lz, electrode spacing and contact sizes are not reported.

concerns.concern: Only one specimen per condition from a single batch was measured, with no uncertainties on S_SSE, σeff or PF. Comparative conclusions such as the 2× differences and the 630% enhancement are not statistically established.
concerns.quote: All samples come from a single batch with one specimen per condition. The RT-vs-300 °C conclusions therefore rest on n = 1 each.

concerns.concern: Density varies with processing route and is not disentangled from Pt thickness and pressing temperature.
concerns.quote: Density (67–75%) varies with processing route and is not disentangled from Pt thickness and pressing temperature.

concerns.concern: The geometry of the thin-film benchmark is arbitrary: σeff depends mainly on substrate thickness. Thinned-film, multilayer and other composite references are missing from Table S1.
concerns.quote: For planar devices, σeff = (t_NM/t_D)σ depends mainly on the chosen substrate thickness

concerns.concern: No reference sample (e.g., Pt/YIG single crystal) was measured in the same apparatus, so cross-laboratory comparison of S_SSE is unreliable.
concerns.quote: No reference sample was measured in the same apparatus, so cross-laboratory comparison of S_SSE is unreliable

concerns.concern: zT, power density and matched-load output power are not reported for any sample.
concerns.quote: zT (≈PF·T/κ ≈ 8×10⁻¹¹ to 10⁻¹⁰ with κ ≈ 1.9 W/mK), power density and output power under matched load are not given.

concerns.concern: Comparing σeff with undoped Si/Ge or the 'bad-metal' regime is irrelevant to transverse thermoelectric performance.
concerns.quote: Comparing σeff with undoped Si/Ge or the "bad-metal" regime has no bearing on transverse thermoelectric performance.

concerns.concern: Absolute power factor and zT are 7–8 orders of magnitude below good ANE materials, yet the paper claims a 'scalable platform' without a quantitative roadmap.
concerns.quote: Temper phrases such as "scalable platform" and "bridging nanoscale spin caloritronics with macroscopic device integration".

concerns.concern: There is no output-power, load-matching or thermopile device demonstration.
concerns.quote: There is no output-power, load-matching or thermopile demonstration.

concerns.concern: Pt cost and mass fraction are not discussed in the context of scalability.
concerns.quote: Pt cost and mass fraction (~10 wt%) are not discussed in the context of scalability.

concerns.concern: Relative density is computed against the YIG density, ignoring the much denser Pt, so the quoted 67–75% is overstated.
concerns.quote: Relative density is computed against the YIG single-crystal density (5.11 g/cm³), but the composites contain much denser Pt.

concerns.concern: The low thermal conductivity is attributed to interface phonon scattering without porosity or effective-medium modelling, and the polycrystalline reference is taken from literature rather than measured.
concerns.quote: attributed to "enhanced phonon scattering at the YIG/Pt interface" without porosity or effective-medium modelling

concerns.concern: Using laser-flash diffusivity on porous, metal-networked samples needs justification (transparency, radiation and pore corrections) or a cross-check by another method.
concerns.quote: Laser-flash diffusivity on porous, metal-networked samples requires justification (sample transparency or coating, radiation and pore corrections)

concerns.concern: Calling the material 'nanostructured' is misleading because the grains are µm-scale.
concerns.quote: "Nanostructured": the grains are µm-scale.

concerns.concern: 'Sintering at room temperature' is actually cold compaction.
concerns.quote: "Sintering at room temperature": this is cold compaction.

concerns.concern: 'Robust mechanical integrity' is claimed without any mechanical testing.
concerns.quote: "Robust mechanical integrity": claimed without any mechanical testing.

concerns.concern: Words such as 'purely', 'rigorously validate' and 'clearly demonstrating' overstate the evidence.
concerns.quote: "Purely", "rigorously validate" and "clearly demonstrating": should be moderated.

concerns.concern: The phrase 'micrometer-scale Pt channels' formed from 15–30 nm coatings is unclear.
concerns.quote: The phrase "micrometer-scale Pt channels" from 15–30 nm coatings needs clarification.

concerns.concern: The text cites the wrong geometry label when comparing the Fig. 3e result (Hx-∇zT instead of Hz-∇xT).
concerns.quote: The text says the Fig. 3e result agrees with "Hx-∇zT (Fig. 3c)"; this should read Hz-∇xT.

concerns.concern: FePt and Y₂O₃ are assigned the same PDF card number.
concerns.quote: FePt and Y₂O₃ are assigned the same PDF card (#43-0661).

concerns.concern: The Cu-Kα wavelength differs between Methods and Note S2.
concerns.quote: The Cu-Kα wavelength is 0.15406 nm in Methods but 0.15418 nm in Note S2.

concerns.concern: Note S2 cites the XRD data as Fig. S2 instead of Fig. S3.
concerns.quote: Note S2 cites XRD as "Fig. S2"; this should be Fig. S3.

concerns.concern: The '630% higher' power-factor comparison is ambiguous, since the ratio is about 7.3×.
concerns.quote: The "630% higher" PF comparison is ambiguous, since 5.1/0.7 ≈ 7.3×.

concerns.concern: The Author Contributions mention VSM, while Methods describe SQUID-MPMS.
concerns.quote: The Author Contributions mention VSM while Methods describe SQUID-MPMS.

concerns.concern: The Fig. S4 caption describes dashed lines only in panels (b)–(c), though they also appear in (d)–(e).
concerns.quote: The Fig. S4 caption describes dashed lines only in panels (b)–(c), though they also appear in (d)–(e).

concerns.concern: There are typos ('Galosov' for 'Golosov', 'worth nothing' for 'worth noting'), and the author name order 'Hirata Keisuke' should be checked.
concerns.quote: "Galosov" should be "Golosov", and "It is worth nothing" should be "It is worth noting".
